instantiated_cells.justification: The statute defines a 'lobbyist' as an individual who receives $2,000 or more in economic consideration in a calendar month (excluding reasonable travel reimbursements) for influencing legislative or administrative action.

unscoreable_emissions.reason: The bundled text defines 'lobbyist' based on compensation/principal duties (Gov't Code § 82039) but does not provide any lobbyist-definition expenditure-spending threshold for registration.
The bundled text does not define a lobbyist using a quantified time standard (e.g., hours or percentage); § 82039 uses 'principal duties' but provides no measurable time threshold.

The bundled provisions on lobbyist/lobbying-firm reporting (e.g., §§ 86112-86116) require reporting of activity expenses but do not state any per-item de minimis/itemization threshold below which expenses need not be listed.

The bundled text includes a principal-side filing trigger at $5,000/quarter for persons making 'payments to influence' (§ 86115(b)), but it does not provide an overall de minimis exemption threshold of total lobbying expenditures below which a filer otherwise required to file is exempt from filing entirely.

No provision in the bundled text creates a lobbyist-side exemption from filing based on spending less than a specified percentage of compensated time on lobbying; the only percentage mentioned is for employer reporting of payments to employees who spend 10% or more of their compensated time (§ 86116(h)(1)), not a filing exemption for lobbyists.
